summary: Describes an optimization for OSPF database exchange in OSPFv2 and OSPFv3. A router skips listing an LSA in Database Description packets if the neighbor already listed the same or a newer instance. It stays compatible and cuts overhead by about half in large networks. It is informational.

eli5.summary: When two people compare lists, you do not need to read out items the other already mentioned. This saves a lot of repeated talk.

questions: what is the ospf database exchange optimization
what is a database description packet
subtitle: A backward-compatible trick that roughly halves the LSA headers OSPF routers send when they synchronize.

tldr.problem: When two OSPF routers become adjacent, each lists every LSA header in Database Description packets, even those the neighbor already has.
tldr.mechanism: A router removes an LSA from its Database summary list when the neighbor has already listed the same or a more recent instance of it, so it never sends that header.
tldr.outcome: This reduces Database Description overhead by about 50% in large, nearly synchronized networks, without affecting synchronization. It is Informational and later updated by RFC 9454.

today: RFC 5243 is Informational and has been updated by RFC 9454. The unit metadata shows nothing obsoleting it.

sections.title: The Idea
sections.content:
In OSPFv2 (RFC 2328) and OSPFv3, two neighboring routers that become adjacent synchronize their link-state databases through the Database Exchange process. Each sends Database Description (DD) packets listing the header of every LSA in its database, so the other can tell whether it has newer instances to request with Link State Request packets.

The optimization observes that a router need not list an LSA if the neighbor already has the same or a more recent instance, since the neighbor will not request it. The neighbor's own DD packets reveal this, so the LSA is dropped from the Database summary list when the neighbor listed an instance that is the same or newer.
sections.eli5: If your friend already told you about a sticker and it is the same as yours, there is no need to tell them about it again.

sections.title: The Change to Section 10.6
sections.content:
The memo modifies Section 10.6, "Receiving Database Description Packets", of RFC 2328. After the usual checks, for each listed LSA the router looks it up and, if it has none or an older copy, puts it on the Link state request list. The addition is that if the Database summary list holds an instance of the LSA that is the same as or less recent than the listed one, it is removed from the summary list.

This step may happen before or after the lookup, but it must be done for every LSA in a received DD packet before the next DD packet is sent in response.

LSAs need not be listed in any order, but a shared order may speed lookups. The memo recommends increasing lexicographic order of (LS type, Link State ID, Advertising Router) for OSPFv2 and (LS type, Advertising Router, Link State ID) for OSPFv3.
sections.eli5: Each time you hear your friend's list, cross off anything on your own list that they already have the same or newer.

sections.title: Example and Properties
sections.content:
In the memo's example, routers RT1 and RT2 start with identical databases whose headers fit in two DD packets. In the standard exchange each router sends two full DD packets. With the optimization, RT2 removes everything RT1 listed in its first full packet, then lists only the remaining LSAs. RT1 removes those, finds its list empty and sends an empty DD packet. Each router sends only one full DD packet instead of two.

The optimization is fully backward compatible with OSPF and does not affect synchronization, because only unnecessary information is omitted. It cuts the LSA headers exchanged by about half in large networks where routers are usually nearly synchronized when they become adjacent, and is especially beneficial in large networks with limited bandwidth, such as large mobile ad hoc networks.

The memo raises no new security concerns and needs no new IANA number assignments.
sections.eli5: With the shortcut, each friend reads out one page of stickers instead of two, and they finish sooner.
